title: Don Fowler's letter quoting Armstrong on the Dixieland records
summary: The interviewer reads a 1958 letter quoting Armstrong's Satchmo, where he listened to the original band's Livery Stable Blues and Tiger Rag in 1918, and a note on the Louisiana Five.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: All right. This is a letter dated May the 27th, 1958 from Don Fowler, 9441 Southwest 8th Drive, Portland 1, Oregon. It's to D. James, D. James, Nick LaRocca, at 2218 Constant Street, New Orleans, 13, Louisiana. And here's a paragraph that Mr. LaRocca would like for me to read. The other day I ran across an interesting statement by Louis Armstrong in his book, Satchmo. He is discussing his life in New Orleans in 1918, and this is a paragraph. Quote, One day when it was raining like mad, Daisy and I went in the front room listening to some new records I had just bought. New releases of the original Dixieland jazz band, which we were playing on an upright victroler we were proud of. The records were Livery Stable Blues and Tiger Rag, the first Tiger Rag to be recorded. Paren, between you and me, it's still the best. Paren, unquote.
Now read down where he says the other steel in the music of the Dixieland band, Louisiana Five.

I have a record of Virginia Blues by the Louisiana Five in which they play the third strain of Skeleton Jangle as a part of the tune. It's signed, uh, Sincerely Yours, Don Fowler. Is there anything else you want to read?
